stdout_tail:
Both `analysis.py` and `result.json` are written to the working directory.

**Finding:** Using a Random Forest classifier (test ROC-AUC = 0.918, accuracy = 0.824) with permutation importance on a held-out test set, **marital-status** is the single most important predictor of income class (mean AUC drop of 0.048 when shuffled), followed by capital-gain, education-num, age, and occupation. Gini-based importance from the same model independently corroborates marital-status as the top feature. Race and native-country contributed the least predictive signal.

Key methodological choices: dropped `education` (redundant with `education-num`) and `fnlwgt` (a census sampling weight, not a substantive attribute); kept missing categorical values as an explicit "Missing" category rather than dropping rows; used permutation importance (not just impurity-based Gini) as the primary metric since Gini importance is biased toward high-cardinality categorical features; aggregated one-hot dummy importances back to their parent feature for fair comparison across features of different cardinality.

parsed_result.summary: A random forest classifier (test ROC-AUC=0.918) trained to predict income class identifies 'marital-status' as the most important predictor by permutation importance (mean test-set AUC drop of 0.0484 when shuffled), followed by capital-gain and education-num. Gini-based importance from the same model agrees on 'marital-status' as the top feature, corroborating the finding.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: top feature permutation importance (mean AUC drop)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Dropped `education` (redundant with `education-num`) and `fnlwgt` (a census sampling weight, not a substantive demographic feature) before modeling. Missing values in workclass/occupation/native-country (~2-6% of rows) encoded as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped or imputed, since missingness itself may carry signal and row-deletion would waste data. Categorical features one-hot encoded; numeric features used as-is (tree models don't require scaling). 70/30 stratified train/test split, random_state=42. Model: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300, min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced') to address the ~76/24 class imbalance without resampling. Evaluated with ROC-AUC (threshold-independent, imbalance-robust) alongside accuracy. Feature importance computed via permutation importance (AUC drop, 10 shuffles per feature) on the held-out test set as the primary method, since impurity-based (Gini) importance is biased toward high-cardinality categorical features; Gini importance reported as a secondary cross-check. One-hot dummy importances/permutations aggregated back to their parent feature (categoricals permuted jointly, pre-encoding) so all 12 original features are directly comparable regardless of cardinality.
